web_evidence.title: 11/22/63 eBook by Stephen King | Official Publisher Page
web_evidence.note: The publisher's substantial interior excerpt from sections 8–9 is narrated throughout by the story participant as “I,” including his surveillance of Oswald and relationship with Sadie.

web_evidence.title: 11/22/63 (2011) — Vote with a Bullet
web_evidence.note: This scholarly Cambridge University Press chapter explicitly states that main character Jake Epping narrates the story as a whole and binds readers to his perspective.

web_evidence.title: Change the past: A review of Stephen King's 11/22/63
web_evidence.note: A review originally published in the Boston Globe explicitly identifies protagonist Jake Epping as the novel's first-person narrator.

web_evidence.title: King, Stephen Writing Styles in 11/22/63: A Novel
web_evidence.note: The study guide identifies Jake Epping's retrospective first-person manuscript as the story's narration; it also notes one localized shift to third person during Sadie's attack.

web_evidence.title: 11/22/63 Historical Context
web_evidence.note: This secondary analysis mentions a transition from first- to third-person narration but does not establish its duration or an autonomous sustained third-person base strand; a related review on the site says first person dominates.

Searched StephenKing.com and Google Books for additional excerpts; the author site offered opening-chapter audio without a usable transcript, while the Google Books result was for an unrelated book of the same title.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages show Jake as a participating “I” narrator, including sustained scene narration with Sadie and a narratorial action beat embedded among dialogue. The authorized publisher excerpt independently shows the same first-person voice in an interior Oswald/Sadie section, and the Cambridge scholarly source explicitly says Jake narrates the story as a whole. Secondary guides report a singular third-person shift around Sadie's attack, but they still identify Jake's retrospective manuscript as the controlling narration and do not establish a sustained autonomous third-person base section. That localized exception therefore does not warrant ALTERNATING. The only residual uncertainty is the precise extent and framing of that isolated shift, which is outweighed by the whole-book structural evidence.
